column2: Does LR depend on quality of either questioned or reference print?
column5: Ideally, yes. Some formulations have the quality of both prints as conditionals in the numerator and denominator probabilities

column2: Does LR depend on quality of either questioned or reference print?
column5:
Yes, and in a few different ways.

The quality can increase the likelihood that the examiner or the system will place the minutiae in a slightly different place. This usually increases dissimilarity between the two prints and reduces the LR. 

A lower quality print may also show increased similarity to non-matching prints because false features are detected. This may increase similarity to non-matching prints and decrease the LR.

column2: How practical it is to handle, proces and manage miliions and millins of prints?
column5: For this LR calculation in AFIS, all the millions of comparisons are temporary. There is some processing time to complete each LR calculation, but the pseudo-latents are not retained, so it's very practical.

column2: Hi Eric. In your theoretical model the dissimilarity is calculated with latents against latents, does this mean that the LR can be only applied latent against latent - not latent against rolled references?
column5:
No. 
The known print that was identified is distorted to create 1M pseudo-latents (based on the known). Then each of the top non-matching known prints from the database search is distorted to create 1M pseudo-latents (10k each based on the knowns).
Then the Latent Print (from the scene) is measured against each of the pseudo-latents. 

Since each pseudo-latent is created from a known print, we're actually measuring latent-to-known.

column2: In practice, many 1:n algorithms (including Idemia) have “score normalisation” based on the gallery size and/or content, meaning that similarity scores change based on the gallery. Does this mean that the likelihood ratio model/calculation has to be recalibrated/reformulated every time the gallery changes, or are you using 1:1 scores only?
column5:
Currently, the IDEMIA algorithm is only used to determine which 100 known prints from the gallery are used to generate the pseudo-latents. The scores don't matter at this point - only the rank.
A different calculation is applied to measure the dissimilarity, and this does not include the score normalization.

column2: Regarding the certification. Appendix F became meanwhile an overall certification standard for fingerprint devices. However Apendix F was original intended for FIR devices. Do you consider to add an additional clause to Appendix F dedicated to contactless devices?
column5: Hi Ralph. Over the years there have been several attempts to re-write Appendix F (as far back as 2010), but none got much traction.   Most recently, the ANSI/NIST Contactless Working group ratified the data interchange standards which will be incorporated in ANSI/NIST 2025.  Once AN2025 is done, I think it would be a good time to engage the Contactless WG & the FBI to see what would work best for them on the cert (Appendix F 2.0, or Appendix "T", which is the next available slot :-)   If you're interesting in participating in that, please send us an email and we'll make sure you're in the list for the WG.
